This article analyzes the reasons for non-compliance with [[indikator-1b|Indikator 1b]], detailing which specific medical examinations were omitted when the clinical standard was not met [^src1]. The data covers a cohort of 65 patients who failed to fulfill the indicator's requirements, breaking down the exact barriers to a complete diagnostic workup [^src1].

The leading cause of non-compliance is the omission of exactly one examination—specifically an MRI or capsule endoscopy—which accounts for 39 patients, or 60% of the non-compliant cases [^src1]. This stands out as a significant outlier and the dominant barrier to achieving full compliance [^src1]. In contrast, the trailing reasons for non-compliance are the omission of two examinations and the omission of a single gastroscopy, each affecting only 6 patients (9%) [^src1]. Additionally, 14 patients (22%) failed to undergo any of the three required examinations, representing a complete lack of the necessary diagnostic steps [^src1]. 

Because the evidence is drawn from a single dated section, no longitudinal trends regarding improvements or declines in compliance can be established [^src1]. However, the data clearly highlights that when patients miss only one part of the required workup, it is overwhelmingly the MRI or capsule endoscopy that is skipped [^src1].
